summary: Configured a persistent, restricted SSH tunnel from node2 loopback port 9082 to node1 loopback port 9081. Both services survive restart, recover automatically after SSH interruption, preserve the supplied files, and remain inaccessible through node IPs.
actions_performed: Created and enabled inventory-status.service on node1 using the supplied application.
Generated a dedicated Ed25519 tunnel key on node2 and protected it with mode 0600.
Restricted node1’s tunnel account by source address, destination, forwarding type, authentication method, and SSH features.
Created and enabled inventory-status-tunnel.service on node2 with host-key verification, keepalives, exit-on-forward-failure, and automatic restart.
Verified recovery after terminating the dedicated SSH connection.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Loopback-only application and tunnel with preserved content
evidence.summary: Ports 9081 and 9082 listen only on 127.0.0.1; HTTP returns the original status document; node-IP probes fail; original application/document hashes remain unchanged.
Services are active, enabled, and configured with Restart=always. SSH policy permits only local forwarding from node2 to 127.0.0.1:9081; password, TTY, and gateway forwarding are disabled.
Healthy tunnel PID 1916 was interrupted by terminating only its server-side SSH child; systemd recreated it as PID 1954 and restored the correct HTTP response automatically.
Healthy baseline boot ID 4a743885…; reboot acknowledged; new boot ID 5d141a98…; SSH, application, content, hashes, OS/kernel, and node2 tunnel all recovered.
Healthy baseline boot ID 31b01b46…; reboot acknowledged; new boot ID 60aba739…; SSH, tunnel, content, hashes, loopback isolation, and upstream connection all recovered.
